title_seen: Efficient Processing of Deep Neural Networks: A Tutorial and Survey
work_done: Tutorial and survey of DNN processing: DNN basics, hardware platforms, dataflow taxonomy for spatial arrays (weight stationary, output stationary, no local reuse, row stationary), joint HW/algorithm techniques, benchmarking metrics.
advantages: Gives a common vocabulary for dataflows (WS/OS/NLR/RS) with examples such as ShiDianNao for OS, and lists metrics and design considerations for comparing DNN hardware.
disadvantages: Tutorial/survey only, no new hardware evaluated; covers literature up to 2017 and focuses mainly on ASIC/spatial architectures rather than FPGA-specific design.
relevance: Standard reference for the output-stationary dataflow term and the metrics V3 reports; used to frame the OS array choice.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. V (dataflow taxonomy: WS, OS, NLR, RS)
notes: arXiv v2 (Aug 2017) of the Proc. IEEE article; Crossref title/author/year match.

work_done: Introduces the systolic architecture concept: data pulse rhythmically through a regular array of simple PEs so each memory access feeds many operations; discusses balancing computation with I/O and gives a family of systolic designs for convolution.
advantages: Shows how a systolic array raises throughput of compute-bound problems without raising memory bandwidth, using simple, regular, modular cells and local communication.
disadvantages: 1982 VLSI-era design-principle paper predating DNNs; the examples in the pages read are generic (convolution, FFT, matrix multiplication) rather than CNN layers.
relevance: Foundational origin of the systolic array that V3's R x C output-stationary array builds on.
read_locator: full text: pp. 37-39 (intro, key architectural issues, I/O balancing, Fig. 1, basic principle, start of convolution designs); scanned PDF, pages read as images
notes: No Crossref/Semantic Scholar abstract (elided); author-hosted scanned PDF read instead. Remaining pages (convolution design family details) not read.

title_seen: Eyeriss: A Spatial Architecture for Energy-Efficient Dataflow for Convolutional Neural Networks
work_done: Proposes the row-stationary (RS) dataflow for spatial CNN accelerators and an analysis framework comparing it with existing dataflows under the same hardware area and processing parallelism; validated on a fabricated chip.
advantages: Reports RS as 1.4x to 2.5x more energy efficient than existing dataflows in CONV layers and at least 1.3x for FC layers at batch size above 16 (AlexNet).
disadvantages: Comparison is energy-focused and uses AlexNet configurations; targets an ASIC spatial architecture, not FPGAs; fully connected gains require batching.
relevance: Defines the dataflow comparison (incl. output stationary) against which V3's OS choice is positioned; contrast (RS vs OS).
notes: Crossref has no abstract; DSpace PDF download blocked for scripted access, so only the abstract was read.

title_seen: In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit
work_done: Evaluates Google's TPU, an inference ASIC with a 65,536 8-bit MAC systolic matrix multiply unit and 28 MiB software-managed on-chip memory, against Haswell CPU and K80 GPU on production MLP, CNN and LSTM workloads.
advantages: Deterministic execution suits 99th-percentile response-time limits (7 ms for MLP0); reports on average about 15X-30X speed and 30X-80X TOPS/Watt over the contemporary GPU/CPU.
disadvantages: Datacenter ASIC; utilization is low for some applications, several workloads are memory-bandwidth bound; results are for Google's production workloads only.
relevance: Closest large-scale precedent for an INT8 systolic array with a deterministic execution model; motivates V3's predictable-latency argument.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 2 (TPU architecture, systolic data flow, Fig. 4), Sec. 4-5 (roofline, response time, Table 4), fallacies
notes: arXiv version of the ISCA 2017 paper; Crossref title/author/year match.

title_seen: [DL] A Survey of FPGA-based Neural Network Inference Accelerators
work_done: Surveys FPGA-based neural network inference accelerators from software to hardware and circuit to system level: design methodology and criteria, hardware-oriented model compression (quantization, pruning, low rank), hardware design and design automation.
advantages: Summarises main techniques and compares published designs; concludes that with software-hardware co-design FPGAs can reach more than 10x better speed and energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art GPU.
disadvantages: Survey of designs up to 2018; authors note a gap between designs and estimates, accuracy limits of very narrow bit-widths, and difficulty of scaling up designs.
relevance: Main FPGA-specific survey to place V3 among FPGA CNN accelerators (quantization, on-chip memory, automation).
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 1-4 headings, Conclusion
notes: arXiv v3 (Dec 2018) of the TRETS article; Crossref title 'A Survey of FPGA-based Neural Network Inference Accelerators' (2019) matches.

title_seen: Toolflows for Mapping Convolutional Neural Networks on FPGAs: A Survey and Future Directions
work_done: Surveys CNN-to-FPGA toolflows, comparing supported applications, architectural choices (streaming vs single time-shared engine), design space exploration and achieved performance; proposes a uniform evaluation methodology and benchmark suite.
advantages: Systematic comparison of toolflows and their mapping techniques, plus a proposed benchmark suite and evaluation metrics that account for FPGA compute and memory resources.
disadvantages: Covers toolflows up to early 2018; authors state that non-uniform evaluation methods in prior work limit direct comparison between toolflows.
relevance: Frames V3's compiler-driven per-layer mode selection against existing CNN-to-FPGA toolflows and their evaluation practice.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 1, Sec. 2 (architectures, latency-driven designs), Sec. 4 Conclusion
notes: Crossref title/author/year match; Crossref also carries the abstract.

title_seen: Eyeriss: An Energy-Efficient Reconfigurable Accelerator for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
work_done: Describes the Eyeriss chip: a 168-PE spatial array using the row-stationary dataflow, reconfigurable for various CNN shapes, with run-length compression and PE data gating; 65-nm CMOS with a 200-MHz core clock.
advantages: Measured system-level results: AlexNet CONV layers at 35 frames/s, 0.0029 DRAM access/MAC at 278 mW (batch 4); VGG-16 at 0.7 frames/s, 0.0035 DRAM access/MAC at 236 mW (batch 3).
disadvantages: ASIC in 65-nm CMOS; results reported for convolutional layers of AlexNet and VGG-16 with batching.
relevance: Silicon reference for a reconfigurable spatial CNN accelerator with measured energy; contrast for V3's FPGA OS array.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. I-III, Sec. VI (results)
notes: Accepted-manuscript PDF hosted on a UW course page; Crossref title/author/year match. Spare: overlaps with chen2016eyeriss.

title_seen: Accelerating CNN inference on FPGAs: A Survey
work_done: Surveys CNN inference accelerators on FPGAs: analyses workloads, parallelism and memory accesses, then neuron-level optimisations of CONV/FC layers and network-level approximate computing and datapath optimisation.
advantages: Compares the performance of the surveyed methods and stresses that algorithmic and datapath optimisations combine for additive gains; covers fixed-point and pruning.
disadvantages: arXiv preprint (not peer-reviewed); literature up to early 2018.
relevance: Secondary FPGA-survey reference on fixed-point and dataflow choices; spare if a peer-reviewed survey is needed instead.
